Show HN: Grid – A Hold'em arena where your AI agent plays your strategy (Beta)
candidates.raw_content: Hi HN, my friend's team and I have been building a game called GRID, a dog poker game with an AI twist. Under the cute dog graphics, GRID is an arena where LLMs compete, with no-limit hold’em as the medium. You duke it out as a strategist, vibe coder, and bot maker. Why: models get compared on benchmarks all the time, but rarely as my agent against yours in its truest form. GRID is our attempt at creating that arena, because we believe this type of game will exist in the future, as AI becomes as common a tool as the browser. How it works: * Paste a prompt and an MCP config into Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client. The agent waits for its turn and sends actions back through tool calls. * The strategy is text written in the game, up to 6,000 characters. We thought it’d be cool to have a preset, “Play like Elon”, to show you what you can do. * You can change the strategy any time, and it applies from the next action. You can even ask your AI to change it for you, based on what it learns about its opponents’ strategies from the match history. * Free beta. Play chips only. We just opened up the game today and are gathering data on how to steer this ship next. Rough edges: * MCP can be finicky, especially if you refresh your browser while in a match. If this happens and you can’t get your agent to connect, wait 5 min and retry | log out using the settings button at the top left and log back in. Stability is currently our top priority. * MCP also uses a lot of tokens, more than the game should, because every tool call costs tokens. We plan to overhaul this with a new connection type in a future version so it’s much more efficient. * There’s a built-in local model for folks who don’t want to use their own AI. It plays basic hold’em OK but struggles to follow written strategies. If you want to try it, I’d recommend leaving your strategy blank. Sadly, it plays best with no instructions. * House bots fill empty seats. We made this choice so matches happen even when only a few people are online. Honestly, I’m most curious how you’d write a strategy that holds up against everyone else’s agents. And if MCP setup breaks on you, please tell me. We'll be in the thread as long as possible. candidates.title: Show HN: KeepPlain – ask your coding agent why a line of code exists
candidates.raw_content: My code is written by agents now. Git blame shows me the commit and my own name, but the reason for the code is in a session I closed weeks ago. KeepPlain saves your agent sessions. It uses git blame to find the session that corresponds to a file, line, or commit. Then it shows the original request and the reasoning behind the change. It also finds commits made by the user after the agent session and links them to the session. I also try to use the mistakes the agent makes over and over to turn them into rules for new sessions. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and Antigravity. Your sessions are uploaded to my server and are kept private to you. All secrets are redacted on your machine before the upload. I’m sure there will be lots of questions about this. The plugin is MIT licensed and open source. The server is not. Teams can run their own Postgres database to store their data. KeepPlain is free for personal use and teams will pay for it. I am a solo developer and this is early on in development so please let me know where it breaks. candidates.title: We’re going to have 100X more agents in the enterprise working with our data and systems than even people do today. Every AI agent deployment comes down to how successfully they can get access to the critical context to make a decision, do research, or execute tasks. 90% of the data in an enterprise is unstructured data, which means this critical context is living inside of our documents, contracts, marketing assets, research materials, financial plans, design files, and more. Which means we need effective ways for agents to get access to this critical enterprise content to other work. We’re excited to partner with NVIDIA to deliver advanced context retrieval -combining lexical and semantic search in Box- to ensure that AI agents can find the most relevant information they’re looking for. All in a way that adheres to their enterprise security, access controls, and data governance policies, so agents only work with the data they’re allowed to. Great to work with @NVIDIAAI and @JensenHuang on this partnership. Files 🤝 GPUs.
